summary: pulse-Doppler fire-control radar (late Mirage 2000C, to the S5 standard), with NCTR

system_loss_db.note: radome, ohmic, processing, straddle and CFAR losses together (assumed)

notch_ms.note: the main-beam clutter notch, half its width in radial speed (assumed)

medium_prfs.note: medium PRF: a dwell at 8 PRFs to resolve range and velocity (assumed, as for every one)

medium_m_of_n.note: a detection on 3 of the 8 (assumed, as for every one)

high_m_of_n.note: a detection on any of them (assumed)

false_alarm_time_s.note: the mean time between false alarms its threshold is set for: Stimson's for radars in fighter aircraft, "a minute or so", read as 60 s (the uncertainty covers the reading)
false_alarm_time_s.evidence: a false-alarm time of a minute or so is generally considered acceptable

noise_figure_db.note: a receiver of a design in service before 1995 (assumed, as for every one)

class_calibration_db.note: its class (tube): minus the mean of the class's residuals against their published ranges, every radar of it alike, whoever made it: an-apg-68v9 +6.4, thomson-csf-rdi -5.6, n019 +5.4, n001 +11.1, ps-05a +0.3

average_power_w.note: a fighter radar's tube transmitter, the PS-05/A's published 1 kW average, as for every one

stimson.title: G. W. Stimson, "Introduction to Airborne Radar", 2nd ed. (ISBN 1-891121-01-4), p. 144
stimson.verified: the sentence searched in the book itself (Google Books full-text search of this edition, 2026-10-07): "In radars for fighter aircraft, a false-alarm time" and "false-alarm time of a minute or so is generally considered acceptable" both match on p. 144, a control phrase ("an hour or so") does not; the page itself is not previewed

validation.evidence: much improved range of about 150 km
validation.note: a fighter of 3 m^2, the one size its sources state (assumed alike wherever none is given)
